Clean reproduction verified today:

1. Started a session with project directory `D:\temp`.
2. Typing `@repl` correctly suggests the pre-existing `replace.py` — autocomplete itself works.
3. Created a new file `bugtest_new_file.md` on disk while the server was running (equivalent to the agent writing it mid-session).
4. Typing `@bugtest` in the same session shows "No matching items" — no restart in between.
5. Crucially, the staleness is **server-side, not a frontend cache** — the HTTP API itself returns stale data:
   - `GET /find/file?query=bugtest` → `[]` (file exists on disk)
   - `GET /find/file?query=repl` → `["replace.py"]`

A few source findings that go beyond the earlier analysis in this thread:

- `packages/core/src/filesystem/watcher.ts` (@parcel/watcher) only publishes file events to the event bus; **nothing consumes those events to refresh `state.files`** in the ripgrep layer, and the layer is memoized per location for the lifetime of the process — so the snapshot can never recover without a full restart.
- `packages/core/src/filesystem/fff.node.ts` hardcodes `available()` to `false` ("fff unavailable on node runtime"), so any Node-runtime install is affected on **any** platform, not just Windows.
- On Windows, `flag.ts` defaults `OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF` to `true`, so the official build always takes the stale-snapshot path.

Real-world impact — this is the worst part of daily usage: a very common workflow is *"ask the agent to draft `plan.md`, then open a **new session** and `@plan.md` to start implementing"*. Because of this bug, I can't just open the new session — I have to **fully quit and relaunch opencode** first, every single time the agent produces a new file I want to reference. Every agent-generated artifact is unreferenceable until a full restart. This alone makes the tool feel broken day to day; please prioritize.

A proper fix would be incrementally updating the ripgrep layer from the already-published watcher events (or invalidating/rebuilding the search layer after write/edit tools run).

New data point on Windows Desktop -> remote Linux server (WSL): the "Add project" dialog for a **remote http server** still uses the *local* Windows folder picker, so a WSL target is persisted verbatim as a UNC worktree (`\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\ssa`) in the client registry (`%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\opencode.global.dat`, key `server.projects["<url>"]`). The Home list then filters the global session index (`GET /api/session`) client-side via `pathKey` (`\` -> `/` normalization for UNC). Server session directories are Linux paths (`/home/ssa` after realpath resolution) or, when the server resolves the raw UNC against its cwd, the hybrid `/\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\ssa`. Neither spelling survives `pathKey` equal to `//wsl.localhost/Ubuntu/home/ssa`, so the project row renders permanently empty while per-project exact-match requests (`GET /session?directory=<raw UNC>`) *do* resolve — sessions are visible until restart and gone after, because only the registry/selection persist. Note the add flow already fetches the server-resolved project via `project.current({location})` but discards its worktree and stores the raw picker string instead; for remote connections the desktop should either use the server-echoed worktree or a server-side path picker, and/or normalize `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\...` to the native mount.

# Reproduction — Issue #39164

**Issue:** "MCP tools not sent to local OpenAI-compatible models (empty tools array)"
**Filed against:** https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/39164

---

## Environment

- **OpenCode:** 1.18.29 (also reproduced on 1.18.26 and 1.18.27)
- **Ollama:** 0.33.3 (Docker container, GPU passthrough)
- **GPU:** RTX 5060 Ti (16 GB VRAM)
- **Provider:** `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` with `baseURL: http://<host>:11434/v1`
- **Models:** `gpt-oss:20b` (also reproduced with `qwen3:14b`, `mistral-small:24b`)

---

## Symptom

The subagent (`Intern`, wired to `gpt-oss:20b`) receives the prompt but returns plain
text — e.g. *"I can't run scripts"* or *"I don't see a question"* — instead of emitting
any tool call. The agent loop exits after one or two LLM calls with no tool execution.

Relevant log lines (no error, clean silent failure):

```
created ... agent=Intern model=undefined permission=[{todowrite:deny},{task:deny}] cost=0 tokens.input=0 tokens.output=0
stream providerID=ollama modelID=gpt-oss:20b agent=Intern mode=all
llm runtime selected llm.runtime=ai-sdk llm.provider=ollama llm.model=gpt-oss:20b
loop step=0 → loop step=1 → "exiting loop"     (no tool calls in between)
```

Note the duplicated `model=undefined` at session creation and only the two default
subagent denies (`todowrite`, `task`) in the permission field — the agent's own
permission/tool config is never applied.

---

## Control — direct API works

The same model via direct `/v1/chat/completions` with a single tool definition returns
correct native `tool_calls` (proper `function.name`, `finish_reason: tool_calls`), and
completes a two-turn agentic task with 6/6 exact numeric extraction against ground truth.

**Conclusion:** the model and the Ollama endpoint are correct. The failure is specific
to OpenCode's subagent tool-passing path for OpenAI-compatible providers — the tools are
never sent to the model.

---

## Related

- #34892 — `toOaCompatibleRequest` reads `tool.name` instead of `tool.function.name` (tools serialize as `undefined`)
- **PR #34887** — the fix for #34892, **closed without merging** (`merged: false`)
- #21181 — local Ollama subagents return tool calls as text instead of executing them

Yep, I just encountered the same thing with GLM 5.3 Flash in OpenRouter. My session was killed and force-compacted without my say-so.

From GLM 5.3 Flash's investigation:

Verified across all of them — here's how the other harnesses dodge the exact bullet that hit opencode:

Claude Code
- Microcompaction: when context grows, old tool results — including images — are automatically cleared from context and replaced with stubs (docs: "expected rebuilds… clearing old tool results from context"). Your 24th screenshot would evict your 3rd.
- Images carry real token weight in Anthropic's accounting (~w×h/750), so the token-based compactor sees them coming — no token-vs-bytes blindness.
- Client-side downsizing on Read to stay under Anthropic's per-image limits (5MB/8000px) — oversized images fail that one image, not the session.

Codex (verified in codex-rs)
- Ingest resize: utils/image/src/lib.rs — every prompt image is bounded by patch-budget math (32px patches; high-detail = 2048px max / 2,500 patches ≈ 2.5MP, exactly OpenAI's vision-token math), re-encoded JPEG q85.
- Byte-aware budgeting: context_manager::estimate_image_bytes converts image bytes → token estimates, so compaction reacts to image weight.
- Compaction drops images atomically: compact_remote_v2_images.rs keeps image+label as an indivisible unit and sheds the oldest images first when trimming to budget.

Pi
- The most direct answer to your bug — packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tool-result-images.ts normalizes every image entering history (read, @file, extensions, MCP, screenshot tools), with a doc comment describing your exact failure mode: "Oversized images make the provider reject the whole conversation, not just the offending turn, so normalize them once as they enter history."
- Plus threshold compaction (contextWindow − 16384 reserve, 20k kept), 2000-char truncation of old tool results during summarization, and an overflow-retry path.

The pattern opencode missed
Every mature harness stacks three defenses: (1) sanitize at ingest — resize/compress before the image ever touches history; (2) charge images honestly in the context budget — bytes or true vision tokens, not "free"; (3) evict old images as context grows — tool-result clearing, not just full compaction. **opencode 1.18.29 does none of the three** for provider-agnostic paths: images enter history raw, count ~free, and persist forever — so one provider with a cumulative 30MB cap turns a routine screenshot loop into a bricked session. The Pi comment is literally a fix for this; worth pasting into an opencode issue.
Build · GLM-5.3-Flash · 3m 16s

Chiming in from a related issue I opened (#47579) before realizing this thread covers the same gap — closing mine as a duplicate, but two implementation notes from it seem useful here:

1. **The TUI slice is nearly free.** The toggle already exists in the TUI command registry as `permission.mode` ("Enable/Disable auto-approve permissions", category `System`) — it's just palette-only because it lacks a `slashName`, unlike its siblings (`theme.switch` → `/themes`, `model.list` → `/models`). Adding `slashName: "auto"` (aliases like `yolo` to match the hidden `--yolo` flag) to the existing entry would ship the TUI portion of this without any new command surface.

2. **Keybinds have the same gap.** There's no keybind action bound to the toggle, so it can't be remapped via `tui.json` — a `permission_mode` action would also serve the keybind-based request tracked in #40331.

Re: the web UI gap @thedanielmay flagged — agreed the runtime, session-scoped approach is the right cross-surface fix; the registry note above is just the quickest TUI-only stopgap.

I’m seeing the same underlying behavior on the current Windows beta:

- opencode2: v0.0.0-beta-19157
- OS: Windows 11, build 26200
- Active plugins: none configured

Reproduction:

1. Run `opencode2 <directory>` and start a task that is still running.
2. Close or exit the TUI before the task finishes, without deliberately passing `--continue` or `--session`.
3. Reopen `opencode2` in the same directory.

The original task is still alive in the shared background service and appears to continue when the client is reopened. In other words, closing the TUI does not reliably stop the active model run or its tool execution. This is especially surprising because a normal `opencode2 <directory>` launch should not silently behave like an explicit session continuation.

Expected behavior: exiting the TUI should interrupt/cancel an active run, or OpenCode should clearly indicate that the run was detached and offer an explicit choice to resume it. A deliberate resume should require `--continue`, `--session`, or a clear prompt.

The practical impact is that model requests and file-changing tools can continue after the terminal window has been closed, with no visible client attached. This also makes it difficult to tell whether reopening OpenCode created a new session or reconnected to the old in-flight one.

This seems related to the Esc-interrupt problem reported here, but the specific issue for me is that closing and reopening the opencode2 CLI leaves the previous run active in the background.

<details> <summary>Earlier architecture exploration</summary>
I looked into a few ways to fix this upstream.

The root issue is that Auto mode currently happens on the client side, so the server emits `permission.asked` before it knows the request will be auto-approved. Integrations like Warp and Orca therefore briefly think user input is needed.

The approaches I considered:

**A. Client-side workaround**
Keep Auto as-is and debounce/suppress those notifications downstream.

**B. Session-scoped server Auto**
Move Auto to the server and apply it to a specific session and its descendants.

**C. Client-owned server Auto**
Move the decision to the server, but make the Auto authority temporary and owned by the client that enabled it.

**D. Instance-owned/shared server Auto**
Store Auto as shared state on the OpenCode instance, independent of which client enabled it.

I implemented **C**, using a renewable lease so the authority disappears if the client disconnects or crashes.

The remaining scope decision is separate from ownership: for the TUI, my implementation gives that client-owned lease **instance scope**, which is closest to the TUI's current effective behavior. `run --auto` instead gets a **session-scoped** lease covering only that run and its descendants.

I have this working locally with tests. Before opening a PR, I'd mainly appreciate feedback on whether that ownership/scope model makes sense, or whether TUI Auto should also be session-scoped.

I’ve pushed the implementation to my fork in case it’s useful to look at: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/47754 (Opened as a draft PR with option C implemented, so the code is easier to look at than the compare link.)



</details>

Verified against a current beta: this is fixed, no PR needed.

**Source commit of beta-17823.** Published 2026-08-21T17:13:07Z; correlating npm publish timestamps with the beta branch tip (first-parent) on two tags (17793, 17823) points at `ea3e0dde` (2026-08-21 15:49 UTC). The code there matches both symptoms: `dialog.tsx:114` has the `enabled: stack.length > 0 && !getSelection()?.getSelectedText()` guard on the dialog close layer (trapped `esc`), and `dialog-model.tsx:106` filters via `fuzzysort.go(needle, modelOptions, { keys: ["title", "category"] })` (with `skipFilter` set on the picker, so this call is authoritative). No commit touched these files between Aug 12 and Aug 21, so no filter regression was introduced in that window.

**Repro matrix on beta-19192 (post-2026-08-25), tmux harness, `--standalone`, 4/4 green:**

- type `c` -> results listed (Spark, Ling, Nemotron, …), no empty list
- type -> `esc` -> picker closes
- type `claude` -> `enter` -> selects model, picker closes
- type -> backspace -> full list restored (selection appears under Recent)

**Root cause of the trapped `esc`:** the `enabled` guard disabled the whole close layer while a terminal text selection existed, and the copy-on-select handler consumed the keypress. Upstream `cb863b8e` ("dismiss the active interaction with ctrl-c", 2026-08-25 — after 17823's build date, confirmed ancestor of the current beta tip) removes exactly that guard and makes `esc` two-stage (clear selection first, close second). The empty-results half does not reproduce outside 17823; most likely the server-side `location.model` catalogue was empty/partial at filter time in that build (fuzzy over an empty input yields empty, and the `enabled` guard then blocked every exit).

Closing as fixed in current beta. Happy to re-verify if anyone still sees it on a post-2026-08-25 build.
